instruction.text: Sort the clauses into the correct categories.

hint.text: Main clauses are clauses that make sense on their own. Subordinate clauses are clauses that don’t make sense on their own. Subordinate clauses will start with a subordinating conjunction.

instruction.text: Find the main clause in the sentence.

hint.text: Main clauses are clauses that make sense on their own. They can be made into sentences without adding anything.

atoms.a: I like playing tennis although it is tiring.
atoms.b: ((I like playing tennis)) although it is tiring.

instruction.text: Find the main clause in the sentence.

hint.text: Main clauses are clauses that make sense on their own. They can be made into sentences without adding anything.

atoms.a: If Sarah is naughty, she will get in trouble.
atoms.b: If Sarah is naughty, ((she will get in trouble)).

instruction.text: Find the subordinate clause in the sentence.

hint.text: Subordinate clauses are clauses that don’t make sense on their own. They start with a subordinative conjunction.

atoms.a: Even though I am younger, I am taller than my brother.
atoms.b: ((Even though I am younger)), I am taller than my brother.

instruction.text: Find the subordinate clause in the sentence.

hint.text: Subordinate clauses are clauses that don’t make sense on their own. They start with a subordinative conjunction.

atoms.a: You couldn’t finish the homework because you were unwell
atoms.b: You couldn’t finish the homework ((because you were unwell)).
